segments.text: Hello, this is David with the Bozeman Public Library,
this time with an update from the future.
It's been a couple months
since we filmed the training videos,
and there are a couple of updates
that we've made to our procedures here.
The first update is that we will be running the filter
for the laser at four blue dots instead of three.
We are gonna be running this at the higher speed,
and the signage on the filter has been updated,
so you'll want to make sure
that you see four little blue dots, not three,
like we talked about in the previous video.
The second update is regarding material requirements.
For acrylic, we now require that it specifies cast.
There are two types of acrylic you can go out and buy,
extruded and cast.
We found extruded acrylic doesn't work particularly well
in our space due to the smell it produces,
so we are going to be requiring
that all acrylic moving forwards specifies cast.
You can sometimes find that on the item label.
If you're buying online, a lot of times
that's either in the item description,
or sometimes if you're on a retailer like Amazon,
it may be in the item title.
But in some cases, you may also have to dig
into the item specifications.
But somewhere in the process,
it should either say cast or casted acrylic,
and we do need to see that when you check in
to use your material.
There are a couple of retailers that only sell casts,
so in some cases, you may find
that the individual item doesn't specify cast,
but you can find somewhere on their website
that's like all materials sold by a star cast acrylic
or something to that effect,
we can work with that as well.
If you have any questions, please contact the lab desk
and enjoy using the laser.
